content.title: Eid al-Fitr 2026 Moon Sighting in Nigeria: Chaand Raat Date, Moon Rise Time, Crescent Moon Visibility, Prayer Timings & All You Need to Know
content.text: Eid al-Fitr 2026: As the blessed month of Ramadan draws to a close, Muslims across Nigeria are preparing to celebrate Eid al-Fitr, known locally as “Small Sallah.” This joyous festival marks the end of a month of fasting, prayer, and reflection, and is a time for communal prayers, feasting, and charity. The exact date of this celebration is traditionally determined by the sighting of the new crescent moon, which signals the start of the Islamic month of Shawwal. In Nigeria, this announcement is made with great authority and anticipation. Eid al-Fitr 2026 in Nigeria In 2026, Eid al-Fitr in Nigeria is expected to be celebrated on Friday, March 20, 2026, marking the conclusion of the holy month of Ramadan. The Nigerian Federal Government has already declared Thursday, March 19, and Friday, March 20, 2026, as public holidays to observe the festivities. This allows the nation’s large Muslim population to fully participate in the religious and cultural events of the day. The celebrations will include special morning prayers, visits with family and friends, and the giving of charity (Zakat al-Fitr). Eid al-Fitr 2026: Moon Sighting Date in Nigeria (Chaand Raat / Small Sallah) The official start of Eid is determined by the sighting of the Shawwal crescent moon. Chaand Raat, the night of the moon sighting, will take place on Thursday, March 19, 2026, which corresponds to the 29th day of Ramadan. You Might Be Interested In On this evening, moon sighting committees across the country, under the supreme authority of the Sultan of Sokoto, will look toward the horizon after sunset to confirm the appearance of the new moon. If the crescent is sighted, Eid al-Fitr will be celebrated on Friday, March 20. If it is not sighted, Ramadan will complete 30 days, and Eid will fall on Saturday, March 21, 2026. Eid al-Fitr 2026: Moon Sighting Time in Nigeria (Chaand Raat) The search for the crescent moon traditionally takes place immediately after the Maghrib (sunset) prayer. On Thursday, March 19, 2026, Muslims across Nigeria are expected to look for the moon shortly after sunset, which occurs around 6:30 PM to 6:50 PM local time, depending on the specific location within the country. Islamic scholars and local moon sighting committees will observe the sky during this critical window to gather reports and confirm the beginning of Shawwal. Eid al-Fitr 2026: When Will Crescent Moon Be Seen in Nigeria? The crescent moon marking the start of Shawwal is anticipated to be visible on the evening of Thursday, March 19, 2026. Astronomical forecasts suggest that while the moon may be “born” (the new moon occurs) earlier, it will be most easily visible to the naked eye on this particular evening, provided weather conditions are clear. As with any sighting, visibility will depend on atmospheric conditions. Clear skies across the northern and southern regions will greatly aid in confirming the sighting, while cloudy conditions could potentially delay confirmation in some areas. However, the official national announcement relies on verified positive sightings from trusted observers across the country. Eid al-Fitr 2026: Chaand Visibility Details in Nigeria Visibility of the crescent moon in Nigeria can vary slightly by region. Northern states, with their typically drier climate and less humidity, may sometimes have an advantage for clear horizon viewing compared to some coastal southern areas. However, the final and most crucial aspect of visibility is the official confirmation process. The Sultan of Sokoto, as the President-General of the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) , will make the final declaration for the entire country based on verified sighting reports received from various moon sighting committees across Nigeria’s states. This centralized announcement ensures unity for the commencement of the Eid celebrations. Eid al-Fitr 2026: Prayer Timings in Nigeria Special congregational prayers, known as Salat al-Eid, are held in large open spaces called Eid grounds or at major central mosques. The prayers are typically held in the morning, shortly after sunrise. General Timing: Prayers across Nigeria typically begin between 8:30 AM and 9:30 AM local time. Abuja: Prayers at the National Mosque Abuja and the central Eid grounds usually start around 9:00 AM. Lagos: Major grounds like the Dodan Barracks or various local community Eid praying grounds typically hold prayers between 8:30 AM and 9:00 AM. Kano: The prayer at the Kano Central Mosque is a significant event, often attended by the Emir, and usually commences around 8:30 AM. Eid al-Fitr 2026 Namaz Timings in Nigeria Mosques Eid prayers happen in large groups shortly after sunrise. In big cities, mosques and prayer grounds often stagger their start times (like 9:00 AM and 9:30 AM) to handle the crowds. It’s best to arrive early for the prayer and the sermon that follows.Before the day begins, families give Zakat al-Fitr (charity) so everyone can celebrate. People dress in their finest traditional clothes—like Baban Riga or Agbada—and spend the day visiting loved ones while sharing meals like Jollof rice or Tuwo.
